failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: Answers ignored existing evidence, answer-slot, length, or name-form rules, including choosing a nearby topic or True/False instead of the requested entity.

rejected_edits.content: - When a retrieved record pairs a clue with an explicit answer, treat it as strong evidence if the clue matches the question; still check that the answer fits the requested slot and all identifying details.
rejected_edits.target: - Allow for paraphrases when matching clues to context. For multi-detail clues, verify that a candidate fits the identifying attributes; corroborate it with other relevant passages when available, and disregard unrelated retrieval noise.

rejected_edits.content: - Before answering, parse the requested answer slot and all identifying relations or properties, then substitute the candidate into that slot: a state requires a state, a “who” prompt a person, and an event prompt the event. Test the candidate against every clue clause and the complete context. When snippets compete, prefer factual evidence that fits those details; keyword overlap in a title or heading, prominence, or a similar name alone is not enough. Do not return a nearby supporting detail, such as a venue, institution, or work title, or a related entity, example, remedy, or mechanism when the clue asks for something else. Do not add specificity beyond what the clue and context establish.
rejected_edits.target: - Before answering, parse the requested answer slot and all identifying relations or properties, then test the candidate against the complete clue. When snippets compete, prefer factual evidence that fits those details; keyword overlap in a title or heading, prominence, or a similar name alone is not enough. Do not substitute a related entity, example, remedy, or mechanism for the requested answer.
